simple.meaning: עֵט (ʻêṭ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a stylus or marking stick.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Job, Psalms, Jeremiah, beginning at Job 19:24. Its contexts include family line, Torah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֵט (H5842).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: עֵט (ʻêṭ) / H5842 is traced through Job 19:24, Psalms 45:2, Jeremiah 8:8, Jeremiah 17:1 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H5842. et עֵט noun masculine Jer 8:8 stylus (√ dubious; Kö ii. 1, 83 (after older authorities) compare Arabic , sink, penerate ); — ׳ע only construct: 1 of iron, for use on stone or metal Jer 17:1 ( שָׁמִיר בְּצִמֹּרֶן with diamond-point ), Job 19:24 (see also חֶרֶט ). 2 probably = reed-pen (used o roll, compare Jer 36:2 , 23 etc.), ׳ע סֹפְרִים שֶׁקֶר 8:8 , figurative, ע ׳לְשׁוֺנִי מָהִיר סוֺפֵר Psa 45:1 (compare Now Archaeology i. 290 Benz Archaeology 290 ).
